newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Blast hurls passenger from Brazil plane.
newsitem.headline: Blast hurls passenger from Brazil plane.

text.p: A passenger was sucked out of a Brazilian TAM airplane and fell to his death on Wednesday after an explosion probably caused by unidentified chemicals tore a hole in the fuselage, police said.

Police said they found burn marks on the floor underneath the row of three seats which were thrown from the Fokker-100 aircraft after the explosion ripped a six-foot (two-metre) gash in the side of the fuselage.
Authorities stopped short of saying the explosion was caused by a bomb. They admitted however they were investigating the possibility of sabotage.
"It was probably a chemical explosion caused by an explosive," Lieutenant Carlos Zorio of the Sao Paulo Military Police bomb squad told O Globo television.
"I saw the burn marks. Now we need to determine whether the chemicals were explosives," Zorio said.

Police found the body of the missing passenger, Fernando Caldeira de Morua Campos, next to parts of the airplane in a field outside the town of Suzano, 32 miles (50 kms) from Sao Paulo's domestic Congonhas airport.

The Fokker-100, which belongs to Brazil's TAM airline, was on a routine flight between Sao Jose dos Campos, an industrial city 68 miles (110 kms) west of Sao Paulo, and Congonhas when the explosion occured.
O Globo quoted a woman who was working in a nearby field as saying she looked into the sky and saw the passenger falling "like a rocket" after she heard the sound of the explosion.
At a news conference TAM authorities said six of the 60 passengers and crew on board flight 283 were injured and taken to a hospital.
A passenger on the flight told Reuters she heard a loud explosion at the back of the aircraft but did not realize anyone had fallen out.

"I was sitting in the front of the plane but I could feel how I was being sucked towards the hole in the fuselage. The pressure in the cabin fell sharply," said Eloir Cavati. "There was panic and we all started praying, even the flight attendants."
Once he realized an explosion had taken place, the plane's pilot Humberto Angel said he warned Congonhas that he was coming in for an emergency landing.
"It took us around 10 minutes to make it to the airport. The oxygen masks did not drop down because fortunately we weren't flying at a very high altitude," Angel said.
TAM vice president Luiz Eduardo Falco told reporters the aircraft landed with all emergency doors intact and both engines functioning normally.
"We did not have any problems with the primary structure of the airplane in the past," Falco said. "We don't know what exploded or when it was brought on the plane."
Falco said TAM had not received a bomb threat and that there was no pressurized container inside the cabin that could have caused the explosion.

The Ministry of Aviation and the Federal Police said they had launched an inquiry into the accident which comes eight months after another TAM Fokker-100 aircraft crashed into homes in a densely populated area of Sao Paulo, killing 98 people including two on the ground.
TAM is Brazil's top regional carrier and Latin America's fastest growing airline. Last week the widely read Exame business magazine chose TAM the Brazilian company of the year.
